title: Fix inflight KV-cache corruption causing 5xx on batched requests during tenant surge
creator: Maya Chen
description: Summary: Multiple customers reported sudden waves of 5xx and timeouts during high-volume batched requests to the hosted text-generation endpoint. Root cause analysis points to a race in the in-flight KV-cache compaction path: when concurrent batched requests triggered a synchronous compaction while a shard-level swap was in progress, the cache entered an inconsistent state leading to null pointer reads and OOM retries which manifested as 5xx responses and amplified retry storms. Affected paths: hosted batch inference path, KV cache compaction/eviction, request retry middleware. Impact: intermittent 5xx for a subset of tenants under surge (not universal), increased p95 latency, customer-visible retries and duplicate token consumption.
reproduction_steps:
1) Deploy a load generator targeting /v1/generate with batch_size=32 and concurrent tenants (5 tenants) sending bursty traffic.
2) Configure model variant with enabled KV prefix caching and compaction interval shortened (test harness used 15s).
3) Observe memory churn on serving nodes and occasional 500 responses with stack trace pointing to kv_cache.go:line 214. Logs contain 'kv: shard swap null' and 'runtime: invalid memory address'.
observed_metrics:
- 5xx rate spike from baseline 0.02% to 1.9% during surge windows
- p95 latency increase from 120ms to 980ms for affected tenants
- host memory churn and GC spikes correlated with compaction triggers
- retry amplification: incoming retry requests x3 within 60s for failing tenants
root_cause_summary: A synchronization bug introduced in ENG-23340 (shardable KV compaction optimization) allowed a compaction goroutine to free or replace shard payload while another goroutine was still reading the shard index. Under high batch concurrency the race caused transient nil dereferences and corrupted cache metadata, which propagated to request handling and triggered 5xx errors and downstream automatic retries. The compaction path lacked an explicit handover and relied on a weak CAS which is insufficient for concurrent batched access patterns.
mitigation_applied: 2025-02-18 22:10 UTC: emergency throttling rule applied to hosted batch route to limit concurrent batches per-tenant to 8 (temporary stopgap)
2025-02-19 03:45 UTC: rolled back the compaction change from ENG-23340 in prod (rollback tag runtime-1.19-hotfix) to stop further corruption
2025-02-20 09:30 UTC: enabled extra logging on kv shard lifecycle and guarded reads with a soft lock to prevent immediate crashes while root fix is developed
long_term_fix_plan:
1) Replace weak CAS-based shard swap with a reader-writer handover protocol (compare-and-swap + epoch token) to guarantee safe handoff during compaction.
2) Add unit and stress tests that simulate concurrent batched reads + compaction under realistic heap profiles.
3) Instrument per-tenant and per-model cache telemetry for early detection of compaction anomalies.
4) Backfill alert: new SLO alert when kv shard swap failures >0 for 1 minute.
5) Release runtime-1.20 with fix and run canary on dedicated pool before full rollout.
next_steps: Diego: implement handover protocol and internal fuzz test harness (ETA 5 working days)
SRE: maintain throttling rule until canary is healthy (monitoring dashboard link below)
PM: prepare customer communications and postmortem for affected tenants
QA: create targeted stress tests in CI that exercise batched requests + compaction every night
canary_plan:
- Deploy patch to canary pool with 5% of batch-serving capacity
- Run synthetic surge generator for 6 hours, monitor 5xx, p95, memory churn
- If stable for 24h, expand to 30% then 100% in rolling fashion
- Abort criteria: sustained 5xx >0.5% or p95 regression >30%
customer_communication:

- 2025-02-21 16:00 UTC: follow-up with ETA for permanent fix and offer for dedicated capacity credit for impacted tenants

resolution_criteria:
- KV shard swap races eliminated in stress/fuzz tests
- Canary passes with 24h stable metrics and no replication of 5xx spike
- Postmortem published and customers notified
notes_for_support: Support should apply temporary per-tenant throttles for customers reporting active 5xx; reference runbook link and escalate to Diego with request ID and tenant ID. Avoid advising customers to add retries until fix is deployed as retries can amplify the issue.
